measuredBy: honest User-Agent, curl -L, no session, no cookies
method: ADR-015 word for word: fetch the site's OWN search with a query that MUST match and one that MUST NOT match, and judge the RESULTS. A 200 is not a verdict and a non-empty list is not a verdict — results a reader would call useful is the verdict, and the negative query is the control that stops 'no results' being concluded from a search that never searched.

urlMap.method: GET only. No session, no cookies, no browser impersonation (ADR-014).

verdict.basis: Two queries that MUST match each returned 20 rows whose titles carry the queried words (LitRPG, System Fantasy, Progression) — 10 of 10 sampled titles, so these are results and not a page that always lists 20 things. The control query that cannot match returned 0 rows with a 200 and the SAME page shell: 97 498 bytes against 250 980, so the difference is the rows and not a different or broken page. ADR-015's criterion is 'results a reader would call useful', and these are.
verdict.zeroRowEvidence: 97 498 bytes vs 250 980 for the same endpoint with rows. The container is present in both; only the rows differ.
verdict.emptyMarkerOnZeroRows: No results matching these criteria were found
verdict.emptyMarkerNote: CORRECTS the first reading of this same file, written 20 minutes earlier, which claimed NO marker existed. It did: the literal is in the page, inside div.search-item.clearfix > h4.font-red-sunglo, as VISIBLE text, exactly once on the zero-row page and zero times on either 20-row page. The first reading listed 'No results' among the markers it checked and then asserted that no checked marker was present — the list contained its own answer. See SESSION_LOG.md session 12.
verdict.emptyMarkerScope: SEARCH ONLY. It is on /fictions/search. `0-2` measured the BROWSE side and found no marker there, and that retraction still stands: the browse-side claim is about div.fiction-list#result > div.text-center > h3 reading 'There is nothing here :(', which matches nothing on a live catalogue page.

consequences: `supportsSearch = true` for Royal Road is now a MEASURED promise (ADR-015), so `3-1` MAY render a search entry for it and `03-source-system.md` rule 5a no longer applies to this site.

`ReadStage.searchResults` becomes `zeroIsGenuine` for Royal Road, and BrowseEmpty becomes REACHABLE there — on search only. B22 is satisfiable on this site because the site supplies the signal itself, which is exactly what B22 asks for.

The browse side is unchanged and stays `zeroIsBroken`: a zero-row catalogue page on Royal Road carries no marker, so it is reported rather than shown as an empty page. One stage becoming genuine does not move the others; the policy is per stage, per source, precisely so a measurement on one cannot silently become a policy on all seven.
Novel Fire could not be measured at all — see its own entry.
notMeasured: POST vs GET. Only GET was tried, because the GET demonstrably works and rule 5a asks about the endpoint, not about verb symmetry.

Author search (`?author=`), tag search, and combined filters. Out of 6-11's scope: the question is whether the site implements search a reader would call useful, and one working query shape answers it.
Rate limiting, and whether repeated searches earn a 429. Not measured here, deliberately: finding that out by hammering is the thing `17-security.md` rules 5-6 forbid.

Whether the marker changes on a future site release. The test re-derives its presence from the frozen capture, so a CHANGE IN THE CAPTURE is what would be caught — and a change in the live site is not, because nothing re-fetches. That is the limit of a frozen fixture, and it is written down rather than pretended away.
